articles.title: For Data Centers, the Case for a Local Balance Sheet
articles.narrative: This opinion piece argues for the adoption of a "local balance sheet" framework for data center development to standardize disclosure of project impacts and benefits. The author contends that while data center projects generate vast amounts of information, it remains fragmented across various stakeholders, leading to misunderstandings and disputes, as exemplified by a recent case in Fayette County, GA. The proposed framework would provide a common language for evaluating projects by clearly accounting for benefits like tax revenue and jobs, against costs such as tax incentives and infrastructure demands, enabling better comparison and informed decision-making for developers, investors, regulators, and communities. The author suggests that such a standard could emerge from market expectations, where transparency becomes a competitive advantage, rather than through regulatory mandates.

articles.title: Data Center Giant Equinix Ups Its 2026 Forecast Behind Robust Q2
articles.narrative: Data center REIT Equinix significantly increased its 2026 financial forecasts following a robust second quarter, driven by strong demand for artificial intelligence workloads and accelerated data center construction. The company reported record second-quarter revenue of $2.63 billion and net income of $477 million, with Funds From Operations (FFO) rising to $854 million. Equinix's CEO noted that the revised outlook reflects a materially improved market opportunity over the past year, with the vast majority of large deals stemming from AI workloads. The company has 52 projects underway across 33 markets, with capital expenditures increasing to $1.58 billion, primarily for capacity expansion.

This incident follows two other conversion project halts in Manhattan this month, indicating increased scrutiny on such developments.

articles.title: On the edge of the next growth cycle for industrial real estate?
articles.narrative: Colliers' Q2 2026 U.S. Industrial Outlook indicates that the national industrial real estate market is nearing the end of its post-construction-boom adjustment, with occupier demand now outpacing new supply for the first time since the construction surge began. This shift, marked by nearly 59 million square feet of net absorption exceeding 53.4 million square feet of new deliveries, suggests the market is effectively working through the speculative development wave of 2023-2024. The national vacancy rate has edged down to 7.3%, and while rental rates show a mixed picture with a slight national decline, the construction pipeline is expanding again, reflecting cautious developer confidence. Colliers anticipates healthy demand will continue through 2026, leading to a more balanced and sustainable market.
articles.market_intelligence: The South accounted for roughly half of all national net absorption in Q2 2026, with Houston leading the nation at 7.5 million square feet, followed by Dallas-Fort Worth, Atlanta, Los Angeles, and Phoenix. Leasing activity was driven by manufacturing users, third-party logistics firms, retailers, food and beverage companies, and businesses tied to data center development. New industrial deliveries reached their lowest quarterly total since 2016.

articles.title: U.S. Apartment Rents Post Eighth Consecutive Month of Growth
articles.narrative: U.S. apartment rents experienced their eighth consecutive month of growth in July, with the national average increasing by 0.03% to $1,747. This modest rise follows a period of flat to declining performance in late 2025. Despite the typical summer slowdown, July's gains were particularly subdued, indicating a notable deceleration in monthly pricing momentum. While annual rent growth is gradually improving, elevated supply levels continue to temper national pricing.
articles.market_intelligence: U.S. apartment rents were essentially flat in July, rising +0.03% to $1,747. This marks the eighth consecutive month of positive rent increases. Annual rent growth accelerated to +1.0% in July 2026 from +0.9% in June. Elevated supply levels continue to restrain pricing momentum nationally.

articles.title: America's War Machine Is Growing, Sparking A Defense Real Estate Boom
articles.narrative: The U.S. defense sector is experiencing its most rapid expansion in decades, driven by a strategic shift to a permanent wartime posture and substantial government spending. This has led to a surge in multi-billion dollar contracts and a significant increase in demand for commercial real estate, particularly specialized office and manufacturing facilities. Defense contractors are expanding their footprints and breaking ground on new projects to meet the accelerated need for space, with experts anticipating a prolonged period of growth for defense-oriented real estate.

articles.title: Fed Holds Rates In Split Decision As Iran War Hampers Inflation Fight
articles.narrative: The Federal Reserve's Open Market Committee voted to hold its benchmark interest rate steady for the fifth consecutive meeting, a decision influenced by persistently high inflation, a softening jobs market, and geopolitical tensions, particularly the conflict in Iran which has driven up crude oil prices. While markets largely anticipated no change, a significant portion of traders had priced in a potential rate hike, reflecting shifting macroeconomic and geopolitical landscapes that have clouded earlier expectations for rate cuts. Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh emphasized the committee's commitment to achieving its 2% inflation target, noting a "healthy debate" among members on the implications of current inflation, the global backdrop, and available monetary policy tools. The decision to maintain rates allows the Fed more time to assess the long-term trajectory of inflation amidst conflicting economic signals.

articles.title: Newmark Posts Record Q2 Revenue, Holds Guidance Flat
articles.narrative: Newmark reported record second-quarter revenue of $888.4 million, a 17% increase year-over-year, driven by strong performance in multifamily investment sales and office leasing, particularly in coastal markets. Despite these robust results, the brokerage maintained its full-year revenue guidance, citing anticipated tougher comparisons in the second half of 2025 and a desire for more market data given the current macro environment. The company's CEO highlighted its strategic focus on multifamily, especially senior and affordable housing, and its significant involvement in the growing data center market, anticipating continued strong activity in these sectors.

articles.title: BXP Closes In On Next D.C. Office Development As It Shrinks Assets
articles.narrative: BXP is pursuing a third trophy office development in Washington, D.C., potentially at 1133 Connecticut Ave. NW, where it is working with an institutional owner on a joint venture and seeking a major prelease commitment. This initiative is driven by strong demand from law firms for large, high-quality office blocks in a market with limited supply and few developers capable of executing such projects. Concurrently, BXP is divesting two existing D.C. office assets, including Sumner Square at 17th and M streets NW, which is under contract for $63 million, and potentially 1330 Connecticut Ave. NW, as it strategically reshapes its portfolio.

data_points.project_notes: The prior owner's lender, New York State Teachers’ Retirement System, took the keys at a foreclosure auction earlier this year. Redevelopment is dependent on securing a major prelease.

articles.title: CBRE Posts 16% Revenue Growth In Q2 As Data Center Business Shines
articles.narrative: CBRE reported a strong second quarter, with core earnings per share rising 30% and revenue increasing 16%, driven largely by its infrastructure and data center services businesses. The company raised its 2026 core earnings per share guidance, anticipating 23% growth at the midpoint. The CEO highlighted the exceptional performance of data center services, which saw nearly 30% revenue growth, and projected sustained annual growth of 25% for the next five years despite challenges like NIMBYism, water/power issues, and supply chain constraints. This positive earnings report is seen by analysts as a favorable indicator for the broader commercial real estate brokerage sector.
